mechanism: Normalize Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBoC total assets as z-scores vs 252d mean/std; weighted composite (Fed 0.35, ECB 0.25, PBoC 0.20, BOJ 0.15); enhance with short_term_liquidity (30d MA), long_term_trend (252d MA), liquidity_acceleration (second difference), and liquidity_volatility (60d std). Relative balance-sheet growth rates (e.g. 52-week pct_change) used as FX features with RSI/EMA/20d vol into RandomForest return forecasts.
data_needed: FRED WALCL/WSHOSHO/WLRRAL; ECB SDW or EURUSD/Euro Stoxx proxies; BOJ/PBoC proxies (USDJPY, Nikkei, Chinese bonds); daily FX closes; weekly Fed vs quarterly PBoC sync via ffill/interpolate.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD and other FX pairs; D1 MT5 rates (~1460 days); Fed weekly balance sheet; multi-horizon returns 1/3/5/8d.
why_new_for_mis: Macro liquidity sensing from multi-CB balance sheets with acceleration and liquidity-vol sub-indices—MIS can gate risk/regime on relative QE/QT momentum rather than price-only vol.
quote: The key factor becomes relative momentum: if the BOJ expands its balance sheet faster than the Fed, JPY is likely to weaken against USD.

mechanism: Instance-normalize series; multi-scale patches (powers of 2 / parallel conv windows 3/5/7 then patch windows step, 1.5·step, 2·step); MLP/MH-FeedForward per scale; conv+max-pool aggregation across scales into encoder tokens. Training uses MSE plus quantile loss (e.g. 10/50/90th percentiles) so the sensor emits both point forecast and uncertainty band. MQL5 CNeuronTimeFoundPatching replaces replication with multi-window convolution.
data_needed: Multimodal HistoryBars×BarDescr; patch count Segments; embedding_size; OpenCL multi-window conv; quantile heads.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Cross-domain pretrain (stocks, FX futures, energy, temps); trading stack EURUSD M1 in conclusion article; H1/D1 harmonic tags in encoder.
why_new_for_mis: Multi-scale patch encoder plus explicit quantile uncertainty is a reusable MIS sequence sensor for simultaneous micro-spikes and slow trends with calibrated confidence.
quote: Multi-resolution patching makes it possible to capture both scales: the long-term trend and volatility noise.... the model learns to output not only the mean values but also, say, the 10th, 50th, and 90th percentiles.

mechanism: TimeFound patching→TransformerUnit (per-variable MLKV self-attn Encoder + CrossDMHAttention Decoder on last-segment tokens) produces forecast tokens; full Encoder stack (BatchNormWithNoise, ConcatDiff, Mamba4Cast H1/D1 embed, patching, transformer, denorm) is self-supervised then feeds Actor–Director–Critic. Latent encodes calm vs volatile regime shifts without labels; agent recalculates each new bar.
data_needed: EURUSD M1 OHLC+tick_volume/1000 + RSI/CCI/ATR/MACD(+signal); HistoryBars; NForecast; 5y Encoder pretrain then 2024 offline RL.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M1; Encoder on 5 years history; Actor offline on 2024; OOS January 2025 (+26.5%, max DD 58%).
why_new_for_mis: Turns foundation multi-scale forecast tokens into an online regime-state embedding for decision gating—MIS can consume the same latent as a change/volatility context vector.
quote: Market data are non-stationary: their statistical properties change over time, which manifests itself in shifts between market regimes — from calm phases to volatile ones and back again.

mechanism: Hurst H from R/S or MF-DFA: H>0.5 persistence/trend, H<0.5 mean-reversion, H≈0.5 random walk; fractal dim D=2−H. Multifractal spectrum width Δα quantifies roughness/complexity/extreme-event risk; MS-CDE sign of α distinguishes bull vs bear. FMH: under stress fractal structure collapses → volatility rises and liquidity falls. Empirical H≈0.54 DAX, 0.5224 crude oil.
data_needed: Price returns at multiple Δt; MF-DFA generalized H(q); spectrum f(α) and Δα; optional MF-DCCA across assets.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: DAX, crude oil, BTC/USD (MF-DFA fig), S&P (Mantegna–Stanley 1–1000 min), cotton (Mandelbrot); EURUSD fractal examples; general multi-TF self-similarity.
why_new_for_mis: Classical mono/multifractal scalars give MIS interpretable persistence and complexity regimes plus a crisis-linked liquidity/vol collapse cue without neural training.
quote: During crises, the structure collapses, which leads to increased volatility and decreased liquidity.... The spectral width (Δα) serves as a predictor of volatility, market conditions and potential returns.

mechanism: Treat market state like Mandelbrot parameter c: connected Julia (c∈M) ⇒ attracting orbits / mean-reverting anchors; disconnected Fatou dust ⇒ explosive no-anchor regimes. Detect mirror-symmetric price fractals around temporal attractor centers (left/right correlation); inside Fatou region forecast horizon is long, on Julia boundary horizon→0. Planned ML classification of such symmetrical structures.
data_needed: Sliding windows of price; correlation of mirrored left/right segments around candidate centers; future practical detector article promised.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD chart fractals shown (Fig. 8); multi-timeframe self-similarity (hide axis → H1 vs D1 indistinguishable).
why_new_for_mis: Predictability-horizon / attractor-presence sensor flags when local structure is mirror-stable vs chaotic—MIS can switch models at fractal-boundary regime changes.
quote: If we knew the center of attraction (attractor or orbit) in advance... we could easily predict future price dynamics. When located in this Julia Fractal region (Fatou region), markets become clear and predictable.

mechanism: Point-wise tokenization of each bar/tick; SwiGLU embedding; Decoder-only stack with causal MHSA then Sparse MoE: Top-K router activates few specialized experts per token (impulse vs consolidation vs range) plus always-on shared expert with sigmoid gate. Sparse second-layer masked multi-window conv (CNeuronMaskMultiWinConv) skips dormant experts; gradients train router to diversify.
data_needed: Per-step tokens (OHLC, vol, indicators); N experts + topK; shared expert path; OpenCL mask kernels; Huber multi-horizon loss + MoE load-balance aux.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Foundation Time-300B domains; trading implementation EURUSD M1 (15y offline) in conclusion; multi-horizon heads.
why_new_for_mis: Expert activation pattern itself is a live regime sensor—MIS can read which specialists fire (impulse/range/trend) as a discrete market-state code.
quote: during periods of high volatility, tokens are routed to experts trained to recognize impulsive movements, whereas in calmer periods they are routed to those that are better suited to handling trends or range-bound regimes.

mechanism: Shared Time-MoE Encoder latent feeds separate forecast heads for short/medium/long horizons (parallel FFNs). Authors’ inference uses dynamic head scheduling conditioned on volatility, trend strength, or model confidence. Implementation: three forecast models on one Encoder; Actor uses latent via CrossDMHAttention with Critic/Director.
data_needed: Shared encoder latent; NForecast / NForecast/2 / 1-step heads; vol/trend confidence signals for scheduling; account state for Actor.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M1; 15y offline then Strategy Tester online fine-tune; January 2025 test (~2500 trades, PF 1.49, deep DD).
why_new_for_mis: Horizon-head selection driven by volatility/trend is an explicit multi-scale sensing switch MIS can reuse as a regime-dependent forecast mixer.
quote: Depending on volatility, trend strength, or model confidence, different forecasting modules are activated.

mechanism: GM(1,1): cumulative sum of prices → strictly increasing grey series; Theil–Sen median of normalized differences estimates level (order-sensitive, unlike SMA). Linear/quadratic/power trends on grey series yield Grey MA variants; absolute deviations → second GM → Grey std for Grey CCI and Grey Bollinger-like bands. Strategies: price vs Grey MA divergence; dual Grey MA LQ; Grey CCI zero-cross and level filters.
data_needed: Price window iPeriod≥2; Theil–Sen pairwise slopes; optional LS quadratic fit on grey series; Deviation≥1 for bands.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic FX charts in article; EA parameters tuned per pair/TF (not fixed in text).
why_new_for_mis: Noise-robust, small-sample smoother that implicitly encodes trend direction via price order—MIS can use Grey level/width as low-data regime and vol envelopes.
quote: When using grey modeling, even swapping two prices can affect the linear relationship estimate and the final result. In other words, GM can distinguish between upward and downward trends, albeit implicitly.

mechanism: Backtracking Search Algorithm is a population metaheuristic (historical pop oldP, mutation M=P+F·(oldP−P), mixrate crossover, greedy Selection-II) for numerical optimization benchmarks (Hilly/Forest/Megacity). No market regime, vol, liquidity, or sequence sensor is constructed.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic test functions only; no trading instruments.
why_new_for_mis: Full read: optimization toolkit article without market sensing content.
quote: The Backtracking Search Algorithm (BSA) is a new evolutionary algorithm (EA) for solving real-valued numerical optimization problems

mechanism: Adaptive price grid over lookback; per zone forensic: appearances, longest_absence, volume_burst_intensity, exit_velocity. VIC=(V×ΔP×LF×SF)/T² flags institutional sweep. Gap created if absence≥Min_Gap_Bars, appearances≤Max_Time_In_Zone, VIC and velocity vs market averages pass confidence_score. Track institutional_footprint, memory_strength (exp decay × daily cycle), mitigation when price fully traverses zone.
data_needed: OHLCV history analysis_depth; grid_density from range/vol; Min_Gap_Bars, Volume_Impact_Threshold, VELOCITY_THRESHOLD; session LF/SF factors.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: FX (lower VIC thresh 1.5–2.0, Min_Gap 5–10), equities (2.0–3.0, 8–15), crypto (2.5–4.0, 3–8); PERIOD_CURRENT chart; live account screenshot.
why_new_for_mis: Time-gap / exhausted-liquidity zone sensor with decaying institutional memory—MIS can mark void levels and rebound probability after fast volume sweeps.
quote: when large volume enters the market, price moves through certain price zones so quickly that a time gap is created - a period when there is virtually no trading activity in that zone.

mechanism: Estimate natural period P via FFT dominant frequency (OpenCL MainFreq skips DC, max |complex| harmonic) per channel; Adaptive Periodical Patching into cycle-length patches; Flex Projection / flex-resize adapts weights across P≠P′; Encoder with RoPE; periodic parallel decoding clones last encoder token K=F/P times with ω(j)=1/e^j. MQL5 plan: fixed patch count with overlap tuned to P instead of dynamic token count.
data_needed: Univariate/multivariate windows length L; FFT real/imag buffers; reference projection size (e.g. 96); forecast horizon F.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: General multi-source TS (hourly stocks, 15m, daily macro); finance emphasis on scale/regime shifts; MQL5 continuation pending (this part theory+FFT kernel).
why_new_for_mis: Dominant-period from FFT is a direct cycle/regime scale sensor; period-aligned tokens give MIS transferable seasonal structure across TFs without fixed windows.
quote: the model adaptively divides the data into segments whose length corresponds to one complete cycle.... when the scale changes, the cycle length changes as well — and if the model cannot handle this, its generalization ability drops sharply.

mechanism: EMA metaheuristic splits population into elite/middle/beginner traders with balanced vs fluctuating market update operators and sigmoid decay from exploration to exploitation. Benchmarked on Hilly/Forest/Megacity only (37.4% score). Metaphor uses market language but does not sense live markets.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic AO test functions; no FX/equity sensing.
why_new_for_mis: Full read: population optimizer article; no MIS regime/vol/liquidity/neural market sensor.
quote: The algorithm simulates stock trading, where market participants with varying degrees of success employ various strategies to maximize profits.
